Same rules as `validateLoaderConfig` in TypeScript.
144	- **Fail safe**: missing, empty or invalid file = send **nothing**. Any bad entry rejects the whole file. An invalid reload does NOT keep the previous packs (design decision: identical behaviour before and after a restart; Nxeon writes the file atomically from validated data, so an invalid file means something is wrong). The reason is logged at WARN and shown by `/nxpacks list`.
145	- **Reload without restart**: `/nxpacks reload`, and a file watch (mtime/size checked every 10 s). On reload, packs no longer listed are removed from online players (`removeResourcePack`); new or changed packs go out on the next join (no mid-game prompts).
146	- **Telemetry**: every `PlayerResourcePackStatusEvent` is counted per pack id and status, plus sends per pack, in `plugins/NxeonPackLoader/telemetry.json` (flushed every 30 s and on disable, atomic, counts survive restarts; an unreadable file is moved aside).
147	- **Bedrock**: Geyser/Floodgate presence logged at enable, shown in `/nxpacks status` and stored in telemetry `platform`. No conversion (Bedrock clients need a separate Bedrock pack; GAPS finding 14).
148	- **Command** `/nxpacks list | reload | status` (permission `nxeon.packs`, default op; console/RCON always).

151	`applyPackChange(current, change, { urlFor }, inventory?)`: `upsert` (add or update) or `remove` one pack, identified by `packIdFor(namespace, role)` = a UUID v5 of `<project namespace>:<role>` under a fixed Nxeon namespace UUID (stable across versions of the same mod; tested against the RFC 4122 example). Existing entries keep their position (stacking order), new ones are appended; URL is always the immutable one for the sha1; result `added / updated / unchanged / removed / absent` + `changed`. `inventory` is data from a server scan: a known pack owner plugin (ResourcePackManager, Oraxen, Nexo, ItemsAdder, ForcePack, ServerResourcePack) or an existing `server.properties` pack gives a `warn` (not a block; merging into the owner's pack is not built). `serializeLoaderConfig` is deterministic. `serverPropertiesFallback(config)` returns `resource-pack`, `resource-pack-id`, `resource-pack-sha1`, `resource-pack-prompt` (written as a JSON text component; format UNVERIFIED against a real server), `require-resource-pack` for exactly one pack (empty config clears them; more than one is refused).

content.content:
## Cyrus asset slice (R1)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r1` (from `feature/cyrus-r0`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 4.2-4.7 and R1 day 5 (textures); GAPS findings 5, 10, 15 and section D (Style DNA, quality bar). **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** No real model build ran: the build service was exercised only through the fake-CLI pipeline test. Sounds are designed to plug into the same path next (see "Sound slice interface").

**The flow.** Build request -> server-side plan gate -> the build service's AI writes texture SPEC files (the existing DSL, Read/Write/Edit only) -> the service validates/renders/quality-checks them like code (bounded repairs) and returns them with the jar -> the portal re-validates, renders the deterministic pack through the version registry, hosts it, computes the Pack Loader entry and records a revision -> (flag-gated) the worker installs the Pack Loader and writes `packs.json` after the jar install.

### 1. Build request (`lib/modbuilder/create.ts`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{kinds,plan,request}.ts`)
- What is REQUESTED: `body.assets` (`["texture"]` or `{ texture: true }`, a request only, never a permission), asset words the Minecraft adapter's route rules recognise in the prompt / change request (`item_model` -> texture, `custom_sound` -> sound), and kinds the base build already has (a change keeps working on them). Passed through `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` and `POST /api/cyrus/generate`.
- What is ALLOWED (`planBuildAssets`, pure): the R0 gate `canAsset(plan, kind, create|edit)` with the plan from the real lookup `tierOf(userId)` (CyrusPlan + admin override; a lookup error = unknown = fail closed), then the version (`itemModelDefinitions`, 1.21.4+; 1.21.1 is refused with "Custom textures need Minecraft 1.21.4 or newer ... Pick 1.21.4 or newer"), then `ASSET_PIPELINE_READY` (`texture: true, sound: false`). Owner rule: free/Katara no assets, Saka sound only, `all` (= Yakko) sound + texture. Only creating/editing is gated.
- Anything refused is a DOWNGRADE: the plugin is built anyway and one customer-visible notice per kind is stored in `ModBuild.cyrus.assets` (`requested`, `allowed`, `notices`, `projectId`, `namespace`; read by `readCyrusMeta`) and returned as `assetNotices` by the builds API. A change to a mod that has textures, on a plan that cannot edit them, says the textures are kept unchanged.
- For an allowed kind the chain's `CyrusProject` is loaded or created (`rootBuildId` = the chain root), so the build has its reserved `nx_<8>` namespace; a project that cannot be created fails closed (no assets, notice).
- **Byte-identical rule**: nothing requested -> no lookups, no project, no `assets` field; requested but refused -> still no `assets` field. Only an allowed request adds `assets: { texture, sound, namespace }` to the service call.

### 2. Build service (`services/modbuilder/{textures.js,prompts.js,server.js,texture-example.json}`)
- `POST /builds` takes `assets` (`textures.js parseAssetsRequest`): unknown fields, non-boolean flags or a namespace that is not `nx_<8>` are a 400; textures on a version without `itemModelDefinitions` in the service's copy of the registry are switched off (defence in depth; an unreadable registry = no textures anywhere). `/health` lists `features.assets: ["texture"]`. Asset builds are never deduped.
- Prompt: the system prompt gets the `CUSTOM TEXTURES` section only when textures are allowed (otherwise it is byte-identical to before; `PROMPT_VERSION` unchanged, texture builds record `mb-assets-2026-10-10.1`). It covers the DSL (sizes, palette, all ops), Style DNA (transparent background, 3-5 shade ramps lit from the top-left, flat areas, no noise or gradients, one dark outline colour for the whole mod, diagonal tools like vanilla), the checks it will be held to, "original art only", and the reference rule `meta.setItemModel(new NamespacedKey("<namespace>", "<texture name>"))` (no `setCustomModelData`, never send packs from the plugin). The namespace goes in the user turn (`assetsBlock`), so the section caches per version. Example spec: `texture-example.json` (= the golden ruby sword).
- Workspace allow-list: `assets/textures/<name>.json` survive only when textures are allowed. A change build without texture rights KEEPS the base's specs byte for byte (snapshot; edits are reverted, new files removed): keeping is never gated. The model keeps Read/Write/Edit only; `scan.js` is unchanged (specs are data, not code).
- Each round, after `validate()`: `checkWorkspaceTextures` (JS port of `checkSpec` + renderer + quality bar). HARD problems (invalid JSON/spec, file name != `name`, quality fail, more than 24) go back to the model as `repair-asset` feedback; SOFT ones (reserved namespace literal missing from the Java, a texture no string literal references, a foreign `nx_` namespace) once. Bounded by `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS` (default 2) and the overall `MB_MAX_REPAIRS`; afterwards a still-failing spec is DROPPED (file deleted, `assetDowngrades`, a warning and a "Good to know" limitation), never shipped.
- `finish()` adds `assetResult: { namespace, promptVersion, qualityVersion, kept, textures: [{ name, path, sha256 (canonical JSON), spec, quality }], downgraded, warnings }`. Specs are part of the persisted source (`files`, `source.zip`).
- Image: `textures.js` and `texture-example.json` must be in the next image, and the registry mounted at `MB_REGISTRY` or `/opt/mb/app/registry.json` (it already is for the JDK map).

### 3. Quality bar v1 (`lib/cyrus/textures/quality.ts` == `textures.js textureQuality`, version `tq-1`)
Runs on the rendered pixels of every texture (service and portal):

| Check | Pass | Warn | Fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| transparency | only alpha 0/255, coverage 0.10-0.85 | coverage < 0.10 or > 0.85 | any semi-transparent pixel, coverage < 0.04, or every pixel solid |
| palette_size (distinct colours) | <= 32 / 48 / 64 at 16 / 32 / 64 px | above that | > 48 / 96 / 128 |
| contrast (WCAG ratio darkest vs lightest) | >= 2.5 | 1.6-2.5 | < 1.6 |
| noise (grain: neighbour pairs differing by 1-24 RGB) | <= 0.20 | 0.20-0.35 | > 0.35 |
| outline (dark silhouette pixels) | >= 50 % | below (Style DNA hint only) | never |
| vanilla_lookalike | | | `not_run` stub: needs the vanilla texture set on the build host (GAPS 15) |

Calibrated on the existing reference specs: ruby sword and health potion pass; the Glock (49 colours at 32 px) and the frost blades (noise) warn. Golden fixtures: `test/fixtures/cyrus-textures/` (`ruby_sword` pass, `flat_square` / `tiny_dot` / `noisy_orb` fail), plus a pinned render hash. The report is stored with every asset. The vision-model judge and owner gallery are later (R1 day 8).

### 4. Portal sync (`lib/cyrus/assets/{textures,sync,sync-deps}.ts`, hook in `lib/modbuilder/store.ts`)
When the service reports `succeeded` with an `assetResult`, before the row flips to succeeded (a DB error throws, so the next sync retries): re-validate + render + quality each spec with the TypeScript code (the service is not trusted; failures are dropped), `buildPack` for the build's version (**no allowPreview**: 26.x packs are refused until the registry marks them verified), `publishPack` to `selectPackStore()` (a storage error never blocks the plugin: status `unhosted`), the Pack Loader entry with `applyPackChange` (role `main`, prompt "<plugin> uses custom item textures. Accept the pack to see them.", `required: false`), one `CyrusRevision` (kind `generated`, status `passed`, manifest `plugin/<jar>` artifact + `assets/textures/<name>.json` asset (sha256 of canonical JSON) + `resourcepack/<sha1>.zip` resourcePack, engine record with the asset prompt version and toolchain) and one `CyrusProjectAsset` per texture (mime `application/vnd.nxeon.texture-spec+json`, provenance = spec, quality report, PNG sha256, pack sha1, build id). Stored in `ModBuild.result.assets` (`MbAssets`, customer-visible): `status` ready / unhosted / none / failed, textures with their model keys, dropped, pack (sha1, sha256, bytes, format, clientVerified, url), loader entry, notices.
Idempotent: the revision is found by `modBuildId` (appends use `expectedHeadId`; a `stale_head` loser looks again), asset rows are content-addressed, the pack object is immutable. Tested with three concurrent first syncs: one revision, one asset row.

### 5. Install (`lib/cyrus/assets/{deliver,deliver-worker}.ts`, hook in `worker/game-mods.ts`)
After the Mods engine installs/updates/removes a Cyrus mod's jar, `afterCyrusModChange` (worker, same guest connection): `ensureManagedPlugin(nxeon-pack-loader, dependent project:<id>)` with the real engine installer, then upsert this mod's entry in `plugins/NxeonPackLoader/packs.json` (`writeLoaderConfig`, https only, no write when unchanged); a version without a pack drops the stale entry; removal drops the entry and releases the loader. A newly installed loader marks the job restart-required. **OFF**: unless `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` it returns before any DB read or server access, and a delivery problem is only reported, never fails the jar change. Turning that one flag on (after the owner steps below) is the only switch.

### 6. NxLabs page (`lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts assetLines`, `CyrusModView` "Custom assets")
Generated from the current version only: "Includes N custom textures; players accept a resource pack on join." (or "... delivery to servers is not switched on yet, so players don't see them yet." / "... could not be built for this version"), dropped textures, and always "Bedrock players (Geyser/Floodgate) see vanilla looks: the custom textures are a Java Edition resource pack." The studio UI is not part of this slice.

### Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-assets.test.ts` (69: the 8 plans x 6 requests gate matrix with call counting, client cannot force, 1.21.1 refusal, project reuse / failure, keep notice, detection; prompt section absent/identical vs present; JS == TS `checkSpec` on 26 inputs (18 invalid), byte-identical render and identical quality reports on 8 specs; golden quality; pack build + LocalDiskStore round trip, re-sync idempotency, unhosted / preview / dropped / namespace-mismatch; delivery switches; page lines), `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` (10, 6 new: texture build succeeds with specs + section + namespace + Read/Write/Edit only; invalid spec -> one asset repair; ugly spec -> 2 repairs then dropped with warning; not allowed -> no section, file removed, no `assets` in the record; change without rights keeps the spec sha; malformed `assets` 400). Whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite: 811/811 (a first full run had one file-level failure of `cyrus-admin.test.ts` that passed alone and on the rerun: flaky under load, not touched here). `devhost tsc` clean.
- RAN on the throwaway DB (`devhost db push`, then `CYRUS_ASSETS_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-assets-db.test.ts`): 3/3 (real `tierOf` with CyrusPlan rows: free/katara/saka/lapsed refused, all + admin comp allowed with a real `nx_` project reused by the change; sync with the real store: 1 revision, head and last-passing set, quality in provenance, concurrent first syncs; delivery with the real managed service + memory installer + local fake guest: added, unchanged, removed, refCount 0).
- RAN real Test Flights on node-2, one at a time (`tsx test/cyrus-assets-real.ts all --out ...`; raw results `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/assets-r1-flights-2026-10-10.json`): Pack Loader fixture jar + `TfItemModel` fixture (does what generated mods do: `setItemModel(new NamespacedKey(ns, name))`, built with `fixtures/build.sh` against the 1.21.11 classpath, api-version 1.21.4; also compiled clean against 26.2) + the `packs.json` produced from the synced pack exactly as `deliverBuildPack` writes it.

| Flight | Pack | Result | Boot | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1.21.11 b132 / JDK 21 | production `syncBuildAssets` path, format 75, 2 textures (quality pass) | passed 6/6: `nxpacks list` 1 pack with the sha1, `config=ok`, `/tfitem` -> `itemModel=nx_r1fl1ght:ruby_sword` and `:health_potion`, both plugins green | 18.4 s | 875 MB |
| Paper 26.2 b133 / JDK 25 | `buildPack(allowPreview)` in the TEST only (format 88; production refuses preview) | passed 6/6, same checks | 10.4 s | 809 MB |

  No process with a run marker and an empty `runs/` afterwards. Fixture jar: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight/inbox/fx/TfItemModel-1.0.0.jar` (sha256 3930e6a7...85f8).
- **NOT RUN**: no real Minecraft client (server-side only): the pack download, the accept prompt and the textures actually showing are unverified (`resourcePackClientVerified` stays false). No real model build (no paid AI): Claude's real pixel quality is unmeasured (C-texture: a 30-sample eval is needed). No real bucket, domain, customer server or production DB. The real engine installer was not pointed at a server.

### Sound slice interface (where sounds plug in)
Built: see "Cyrus sound slice (R1)" below for what was implemented (one spec file per sound SET rather than per event).
1. `lib/cyrus/assets/plan.ts`: set `ASSET_PIPELINE_READY.sound = true`. The gate (Saka+), the request detection (`custom_sound` rule), the service flag (`assets.sound`, already parsed and recorded) and the notices need no change.
2. Service: a `SOUND_SECTION` in `prompts.js` appended when `rec.assets.sound`; spec files `assets/sounds/<event>.json` (a `SoundSpec`: events -> layers -> processing, library refs by id) added to the `sanitizeWorkspace` allow-list under the same keep rule; a `checkWorkspaceSounds` beside `checkWorkspaceTextures` returning `{ problems, soft, results }`, run by `assetRound` (shares `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS` and the drop-don't-ship downgrade); `assetResult.sounds: [{ key, path, sha256, spec, quality }]` next to `textures`. Plugin rule: play `Sound.sound(Key.key(ns, event))`-style namespaced keys from `sounds.json`, never override vanilla keys.
3. Portal: `SvcAssetResult.sounds`; in `syncBuildAssets` render each sound (server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis mono Ogg), quality (mono, true peak, loudness band, silence ratio), add `assets/<ns>/sounds/*.ogg` + `sounds.json` (with mandatory subtitle keys) to the SAME pack (extend `buildPack` to take `sounds`), `recordAsset(kind "sound")`, manifest role `asset`; `MbAssets.sounds`. Hosting, the Pack Loader entry, the revision, delivery and the page lines are shared (one pack per mod, role `main`).

### Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- Pack entries are `required: false`: a player who declines sees missing-model items instead of being kicked. Change to `true` per mod if the owner prefers.
- `existing` textures count as requested on a change, so a top-plan change can edit them; a lower plan gets "kept exactly as they are".
- Quality thresholds above (v1, calibrated on the 4 reference specs); the outline check only warns.
- Soft cross-checks (namespace literal / unreferenced texture) get one repair and then become warnings, because a plugin may build keys from parts; hard failures are dropped.
- A storage error leaves the plugin shipped with status `unhosted` (no automatic re-publish yet).
- Revision kind is `generated` also for kept (unchanged) textures; `message` says "(kept unchanged)".
- `PROMPT_VERSION` was left unchanged so non-asset builds keep their dedupe keys; asset builds carry `mb-assets-2026-10-10.1`.

### Owner actions (nothing needed to merge; all needed before customers see textures)
1. R0 items first: apply the engine-core and managed-plugin migrations, seed the catalog, choose pack storage + an Nxeon pack domain (`CYRUS_PACK_STORE=s3`, `CYRUS_PACK_S3_*`, `CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE`), put the Pack Loader jar on the worker host.
2. Rebuild the build-service image with `textures.js` + `texture-example.json` (VM 88001 untouched by this branch).
3. A real-client test day (T) on 1.21.11 and 26.x: accept the pack, see the ruby sword; then set `resourcePackClientVerified`.
4. Approve a small paid eval (about 30 texture prompts) before promising texture quality.
5. Then `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` on the worker is the only switch for delivery.

## Cyrus import your own mod (R2)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r3` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`), 2026-10-10. A customer uploads a mod they own, works on it in Cyrus and builds it with Cyrus. **Nothing is deployed and the feature is OFF**: setting `cyrus_import_enabled` (default `false`, in the Cyrus settings catalogue, group launch, marked risky). It fails closed: off, unset or unreadable means every import route answers 404. Import is **not plan-gated** (owner decision); building on an import later goes through the normal change flow, so tokens, the model the plan allows and the asset gates apply exactly as for any build.

**What can be imported**: a source ZIP (one Gradle, Maven or plain module; GitHub-style root folder is fine), a plugin JAR, a datapack ZIP, a resource-pack ZIP (25 MB upload cap).

**Files**
- `lib/cyrus/import/ingest.ts`: safe ingestion (pure, in memory, nothing written or run). Reuses the inventory's bounded ZIP reader (`lib/cyrus/inventory/zipread.ts`, which now also exposes `madeBy`/`extAttr` and `isSymlinkEntry`), its descriptor parser and `inspectJar`.
- `lib/cyrus/import/deps.json` + `deps.ts`: the dependency allowlist and the resolver.
- `lib/cyrus/import/licence.ts`, `attestation.ts`: SPDX detection, the attestation record, the sharing rule, the revision-metadata validator.
- `lib/cyrus/import/store.ts`: the quarantine store (injectable; `FsQuarantine` at `CYRUS_IMPORT_DIR`, default `/var/lib/nxeon/cyrus-imports`, files 0600 in a 0700 dir, named by the opaque import id; `MemoryQuarantine` for tests).
- `lib/cyrus/import/importer.ts`: `importMod`, `getImport`, `listImports`, `deleteImport`, `checkImportConflicts`, behind the `ImporterDeps` host seam.
- `lib/cyrus/import/api.ts`: the framework-free HTTP layer; `deps-db.ts` (DB half) and `deps-real.ts` (today's Nxeon wiring: settings flag, rate limiter, signed-in Cyrus user, build-service client, read-only server view through the Mods engine GuestFs, the same adapter `lib/modbuilder/install.ts` uses).
- Routes: `GET|POST /api/cyrus/import`, `GET|DELETE /api/cyrus/import/:projectId`, `POST /api/cyrus/import/:projectId/conflicts {serverId}`.
- Service: `services/modbuilder/import.js` (re-validation, allowlisted classpath, docs as data), `scan.js` profiles, `server.js` `POST /imports` + `runImport`, `prompts.js` import variants, `tools/fetch-import-deps.js`, Dockerfile lines (inert until an image is built).
- Tests: `test/cyrus-import.test.ts` (pure), `test/cyrus-import-api.test.ts` (routes + importer with fakes), `test/modbuilder-import-pipeline.test.ts` (real server.js, fake CLI/javac/javap), `test/cyrus-import-db.test.ts` (throwaway DB, opt-in `CYRUS_IMPORT_DB_TEST=1`), `test/cyrus-import-real.ts` (node-2 real runs, not in the suite). Fixtures in `test/fixtures/cyrus-import/` (`demo-src`, `evil-src`, `scan-src` + `javap` = real javac/javap output).

**Ingestion (in this order; refused before anything is inflated)**: upload size; entry count (5,000); names: traversal, absolute, backslash, drive letters, NUL/control characters, `.` segments, depth over 40, segments over 255 chars, names over 400 bytes; duplicate paths (exact or differing only by case); symbolic links (Unix `S_IFLNK` in the external attributes); encrypted and zip64 entries; declared inflated total over 96 MB; archive ratio over 40:1 (past 8 MB); per-entry ratio over 100:1 (entries over 64 KB); entries over 8 MB. While reading: one shared inflate budget for the upload and every nested archive, CRC check, `maxOutputLength` so a lying header cannot allocate past its size. Nested archives at most 2 deep (a zip holding a single jar is unwrapped once). Fuzz test: 400 random mutations never throw and never yield an unsafe kept path.

Source ZIP: only `src/main/java/**.java` and `src/main/resources/**` (data file types: yml, json, properties, txt, lang, png, ogg, nbt, ...) of the module that holds `plugin.yml` are kept. **The uploader's build files (`build.gradle*`, `settings.gradle*`, `gradle.properties`, `gradlew*`, `pom.xml`, `mvnw*`, `gradle/`, `.mvn/`, `buildSrc/` ...) are read as text for detection only, dropped, listed to the user and never run**; bundled jars are ignored; `src/test`, IDE and CI files are left out. Detected: build system, descriptor, name/version/main/api-version, commands, permissions, (soft)depends, language, whether the sources are complete (main class present; every import under the main package resolves to an uploaded class), dependencies (build-file coordinates, plugin.yml depends, Java imports). Refused with `unsupported: X` and the reason: Kotlin, Scala, Groovy, Lombok (import or build), annotation processors (build config or a `javax.annotation.processing.Processor` service file), `module-info.java`, `paper-plugin.yml` (Paper's experimental format; its loader can fetch libraries at runtime), a `plugin.yml` `libraries:` section (runtime Maven downloads), names Cyrus does not build (spaces), code or archives in resources, non-Java code in `src/main/java`, multi-module projects where several or no modules have a descriptor, incomplete sources, and any import that is not JDK, Paper, own source or allowlisted (`unsupported dependency: X` + how to request it). Build-file coordinates the code never imports are only a note.

Plugin JAR: analysis and diagnosis only. Descriptor and bytecode summary from the inventory reader; class-major check (65 for 1.21.x, 69 for 26.x); server jars refused; signature files (`*.SF/RSA/DSA/EC`, `SIG-*`) stripped from what is handled and reported; multi-release noticed (versioned classes are analysed too); nested archives vetted for depth and bombs. Cyrus never claims a jar can be safely modified, never rebuilds it and never decompiles it into shared knowledge (no decompiler is used at all yet).

Datapack / resource pack: `pack.mcmeta` with a `pack_format`, files of data types inside the pack tree only, shader overrides noted; code or archives refused.

**Attestation + licence** (`attestation.ts`, pure): the upload needs the box ticked, the CURRENT text version (`cyrus-import-attest-2026-10-10.1`) and a typed name (2-100 chars, control characters stripped). The record `{textVersion, typedName, at, uploadSha256, detectedLicences, detected, claimedLicence}` lives in the imported revision's metadata (`CyrusRevision.engine.import`, strictly validated by `validateImportMeta`; no new table). Licences are detected from `SPDX-License-Identifier` headers, LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE/UNLICENSE wording and POM `<licenses>`; "unknown" is a valid answer. **Sharing rule** (`mayShareImport`): public sharing needs explicit consent (`cyrus-import-share-2026-10-10.1`) AND a licence that permits redistribution; unknown, a detected/claimed conflict, several detected licences, or "All rights reserved" => private only; copyleft (GPL/LGPL/AGPL/MPL/EPL) also needs the source published; jar-only imports are never shared. Nothing in the publishing flow calls it yet (no import can be published today); it is the rule the publish gate must call.

**Dependency allowlist** (`deps.json`, version `cyrus-import-deps-2026-10-10.1`). Every jar was downloaded from its official repository into node-2 `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-import-deps` and its SHA-1 matched the repository's published `.sha1`; the service re-verifies the sha256 before every compile. All are **compile-only, never shaded** (the server must run the real plugin):

| id | coordinates | licence | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| vault-api | com.github.MilkBowl:VaultAPI:1.7 (jitpack) | LGPL-3.0 | 47f6a400...2601 |
| luckperms-api | net.luckperms:api:5.5 (Maven Central) | MIT | cd910f93...294f |
| placeholderapi | me.clip:placeholderapi:2.11.6 (repo.extendedclip.com) | GPL-3.0 | b20cb09d...dffd |
| protocollib | com.comphenix.protocol:ProtocolLib:5.3.0 (repo.dmulloy2.net) | GPL-2.0 | 1e10c499...78b9 |

Provided by Paper (no entry needed): paper/spigot/bukkit API, Adventure, Gson, SnakeYAML, Guava, JetBrains annotations, JSR-305, checker-qual, jspecify, Brigadier, JOML, fastutil, SLF4J, Log4j API, BungeeCord chat, commons-lang3. Refused with reasons: bStats (must be shaded: copy its MIT `Metrics` class into your source instead, which the attested profile then reports as an HTTP warning), Lombok, Kotlin, NMS/CraftBukkit/paperweight, processor libraries (auto-service, auto-value, MapStruct, Dagger, Immutables), other platforms (Velocity, BungeeCord plugin API, Sponge, Fabric, Forge, NeoForge). Candidates to add next (need their transitive API jars resolved first): WorldGuard/WorldEdit, EssentialsX, Citizens.

**Scan profiles** (`services/modbuilder/scan.js`). `strict` is the default and exactly the previous rules (all existing scan tests unchanged; the default system prompt hash is unchanged too). `attested` is only for code its owner uploaded and attested: it runs the same rules over every RAW finding (before de-duplication, so one class with an HTTP call and a raw socket keeps the socket block), then downgrades only these from block to warning:

| rule | becomes | only when | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| network | network-http | every java.net/javax.net type on the line is URL, URLConnection, HttpURLConnection, HttpsURLConnection, java.net.http.* or a value type | update checkers and bStats-style metrics; raw sockets, server sockets, datagrams, socket channels, URLClassLoader stay blocked |
| reflection | reflection-lookup | not MethodHandles.lookup/privateLookupIn, Lookup.find*/unreflect*, MethodHandle.invoke, VarHandle | Class.forName / getDeclared* / Method.invoke for version, Folia and command-map checks |
| jndi-rmi-jmx | database | DriverManager / javax.sql only | SQLite/MySQL storage through JDBC; JNDI, RMI, JMX stay blocked |
| load-plugins | disable-plugin | PluginManager.disablePlugin only | self-disable when a dependency is missing; load/enable/clear plugins stays blocked |
| class-name-string | internals-name | the text names org.bukkit.craftbukkit / net.minecraft.server only | server-version detection; text naming Runtime, ProcessBuilder, class loaders, reflection, JNDI ... stays blocked |

It also lists the web addresses the code names (`network-endpoint`, up to 10). Hard blocks in both profiles: process execution, shell/scripts/compilers, loading code at runtime (class loaders, instrumentation, JarFile/ZipInputStream, ServiceLoader, deserialisation), raw networking, DNS lookups, JNDI/RMI/JMX, Unsafe/JVM internals, MethodHandles tricks, exit/halt, JVM-wide settings, JNI, NMS, plugin loading, and every source rule (files outside the plugin folder, hard-coded secrets, Nxeon paths, encoded blobs, privileged hard-coded players). An unknown profile name throws (a typo never weakens the scan). The attested profile never says "safe": reports say `Checked with the attested profile: N warnings`, the build's first warning says Nxeon checked it but does not guarantee it is safe, the verdict is `warn` even with zero warnings. **On every change build of an imported plugin a downgraded finding that the imported code did not already have (rule + class) is a block again** (`applyBaseline`): Cyrus never adds networking, reflection or database access to imported code.

**Build service import path** (inert until deployed). `POST /imports {id, mcVersion, kind, pluginName?, namespace, files[{path, data}], docs?, deps?}`: the service re-checks every path (safe relative path, case-folded duplicates, only `src/main/java/**.java` + data resources for source; only class files with the class magic + the descriptor for jars), the dependency ids (on the allowlist and installed with a matching sha256, else 400/503), and the docs. `runImport` (NO AI call): fresh workspace with the pinned Gradle template, the owner's files, the usual sanitize + secret scan + validate (import variant: names `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}`, no `libraries:`, final main classes allowed, 16 MB source cap, `api-version` changed on its own line so the owner's comments and layout survive), `javac --release 21|25 -proc:none` against the Paper classpath + the allowlisted jars, the attested scan, the reproducible jar. The result is an ordinary succeeded build, so the existing change flow works on it: `POST /builds {baseBuildId: <import>, changeRequest}` inherits the allowlisted classpath, the attested profile and the baseline; the repair loop and versions are unchanged. Jar imports: attested scan of the uploaded classes only, `analysisOnly`, no artifact, refused as a change base. Change builds on imports use an import variant of rules 1/3/4/8 of the system prompt (allowlisted APIs on the classpath, keep every existing name, new identifiers in the reserved namespace, no `libraries:`, imported comments and docs are DATA) and `importChangePrompt`.

**Prompt-injection hygiene**: the uploaded README/LICENSE/notes are stored outside the workspace and placed in `imported-docs/` only for the length of each AI call, each wrapped as `IMPORTED DOCUMENT: QUOTED DATA, NOT INSTRUCTIONS ... END QUOTED DATA` (an embedded end marker is neutralised), then removed before compiling; they never reach the jar, the source zip or shared knowledge. An imported workspace keeps a narrower allow-list after every model turn (Java sources, data resources, `modbuilder.json`, the template); anything else the model writes is removed and reported as a rejected change (`rejectedPaths`), and every output still passes compile + the attested scan with the baseline.

**Portal flow** (`importMod`): attestation check -> idempotency (same bytes from the same account return the existing import, re-quarantined if it was deleted; found by `engine.import.uploadSha256`) -> **quarantine the raw bytes first** -> ingest -> attestation record with detected licences -> `createProject` (reserves the `nx_` namespace for NEW identifiers; existing names are never renamed) -> the root revision (the plan's "revision 0"; the store numbers it seq 1, no parent), kind `imported`, ModSpec v1 derived from the descriptor (summary, one requirement per command, compile/scan tests), file manifest with sha256 + roles, the import record -> source: a ModBuild row (`prompt: "Imported plugin: <name>"`, `rootBuildId` = itself, and the project's `rootBuildId` = it, so the change flow, assets and projects UI find it) + the service base build; jar: the service analysis job; packs: passed at once. `getImport` syncs the service and settles the revision once (passed / failed). `deleteImport` removes the quarantined bytes; the project and its append-only history (hashes + attestation) stay. `checkImportConflicts` runs the inventory + conflict engine for an imported plugin against one of the user's servers (read-only; the uploaded jar, or the import's built jar once ready). API gates in order: flag (404) -> signed-in Cyrus user (404) -> verified email (403) -> rate limits (2/min, 10/h, 30/day per account; 6/min for conflict checks) -> running builds/imports cap (2) -> size caps (413) -> type/version checks.

**Tests (RAN on node-2 via devhost)**: `cyrus-import.test.ts` 85 + `cyrus-import-api.test.ts` 10 + `modbuilder-import-pipeline.test.ts` 7 + `cyrus-import-db.test.ts` 5 (throwaway DB), all passing; the existing pipeline, scan, inventory, engine-core, conflicts, modpack, assets, sounds, efficiency and live suites still pass (418 together). `tsc` clean. `test/cyrus-admin.test.ts` fails the same way on the base branch (a server-only import), unrelated.

**REAL runs on node-2** (`scripts/devhost run --lock -- npx tsx test/cyrus-import-real.ts`; raw results `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/import-r2-real-2026-10-10.json`). No real game client and no AI model were used (the import path makes no model call). The four allowlist jars re-verified (sha256 + sha1 + size). The REAL `services/modbuilder/server.js` ran on node-2 with JDK 21 (Test Flight's Temurin 21.0.12.1) and, for 26.2, JDK 25 (a test-only registry copy marked 26.2 buildable; the shipped registry still says preview), the resolved Paper classpaths, the allowlisted jars, and `yaml@2.8.1` installed into `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-import-real/svcdeps` (npm sha512 integrity matched the registry). The fixture project (`test/fixtures/cyrus-import/demo-src`: Vault economy hook, PlaceholderAPI expansion, a bStats-style HTTPS metrics class, a Spigot update checker, a command with a reload subcommand, a join listener, config.yml, a Gradle build with a malicious `steal` task, gradlew, a README with a prompt-injection comment, an MIT LICENSE) went through the portal ingestion (build files dropped, deps = placeholderapi + vault-api) and `POST /imports`:
- 1.21.11: succeeded in 1.7 s; `Checked with the attested profile: 5 warnings` (reflection-lookup and network-http in Metrics, network-http in UpdateChecker, two network-endpoint), **no blocks**; jar 10,250 bytes, class major 65, no shaded dependency classes, no build files, the author's plugin.yml comment kept; the same import again gave the same jar sha256 (reproducible).
- 26.2: succeeded in 1.6 s with the same 5 warnings; class major 69; reproducible.
- `evil-src` (Runtime.exec from a command): failed `safety`, `block:exec@me.demo.evil.EvilImport`.
- Test Flight (one at a time; node-2 was busy with another agent's flight three times and the backoff waited): 1.21.11 **passed** (boot 18.1 s; plugins enabled, startup log clean, `/plugins` lists ImportDemo, `/importdemo` and `/importdemo reload` answer, clean stop, no leaks); 26.2 **passed** with the 26.2 build (boot 11.0 s, same 6 checks).

**Design decisions the plan did not specify**: the root revision is seq 1 (the store's numbering) and is what the plan calls revision 0; jar-only and pack imports have no ModBuild row (they cannot be changed, so nothing would use one); import compile errors fail the import with the compiler output (no AI repair at import; ask Cyrus after importing a version that compiles); raw sockets, JarFile and encoded blobs stay blocked even for owned code; bStats is refused as a dependency (must be shaded) but its copied-in source is fine; build-file-only dependencies are notes, imports are what count; idempotency is by upload hash per account and is sequential (two simultaneous identical uploads could still make two projects; the per-minute limit makes it rare); `deleteImport` keeps the history; the conflict check replaces an older copy of the same plugin on the server rather than reporting it as a clash.

**Owner actions / decisions**: (1) review the attestation and share-consent wording (bump the version constants when changed); (2) rate limits and the 25 MB cap; (3) enabling `cyrus_import_enabled` (only after the build-service image has `import.js`, `deps.json` + the verified jars in `/opt/mb/deps` and the deploy); (4) the VM image change: copy `lib/cyrus/import/deps.json` next to the Dockerfile and rebuild (the image build fetches and verifies the jars; the Dockerfile's app COPY line also still lacks the R1 `textures.js`/`sounds.js` files, check before rebuilding); (5) which further dependencies to allowlist; (6) whether GPL dependencies (PlaceholderAPI, ProtocolLib) need a note to users about their own plugin's licence; (7) quarantine retention (nothing expires uploads yet).

## Cyrus sound slice (R1)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r1` (2026-10-10), on top of the asset slice above. MASTER-PLAN 4.7 (Sound, Saka+) and R1 day 6. **Nothing is deployed or switched on**: sound rendering is OFF unless `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh`, the owner's library is OFF for customer builds unless `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`, and delivery still needs `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1`. No real model build ran; no client heard anything.

**The flow.** Build request (plan gate: sound = Saka and the top plan) -> the service's AI writes SoundSpec files `assets/sounds/<set>.json` (one SET per mob/item/spell, events inside) -> the service validates them like code (bounded repairs, drop-don't-ship) and returns them in `assetResult.sounds` -> the portal re-validates (library licence policy, budgets) and sends a render job (specs + library refs, NO audio) to the RENDER HOST (node-2) -> node-2 decodes library MP3s, runs the pure DSP chain, encodes mono Ogg Vorbis, decodes it back and runs the quality bar -> the portal checks every returned file (sha256, `OggS`, mono Vorbis, verdict) and adds `sounds.json` + subtitles + the Oggs to the SAME pack as the textures -> hosting, Pack Loader entry, revision and delivery are shared with textures (one pack per mod).

### 1. Library (`lib/cyrus/sound/{library,library-search,classify,descriptors}.ts`, `taxonomy.json`, `library.manifest.json`)
- The owner's zip (`board-uploads/.../819080d91d471a0eceeab422.zip`, sha256 `5796b4ac...86c9`, 514 MP3 + 1 PDF) was copied to node-2 and extracted to `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/sound-library/files` (read-only, dir mode 700). **No audio is in git, in /opt/nxeon or in any served directory**; a test fails if an audio file is tracked.
- `library.manifest.json` (metadata only, generated by `scripts/cyrus/sound-manifest.ts` from two scans run ON node-2: `scan.py`-style ffprobe + ebur128/astats, and `scripts/cyrus/sound-descriptors.ts`): per file a stable id `<slug>_<4 hex of the content sha256>`, file name, prefix, category, use cases, tags, descriptors, raw measurements (centroid, attack, front energy, start/end level, crest), duration, sample rate (455 x 44.1 kHz, 59 x 48 kHz), channels (all stereo), bit rate, LUFS, true/sample peak, RMS, DC, sha256, and a **ledger row**: `provenance: owner-provided (2026-10-10)`, `licenceStatus: unverified: owner to document source per file group`. Originality is never asserted.
- **Licence finding**: the zip contains `_Essential Sound Effects Bundle License.pdf` (sha256 `ab1a9796...0db3`) naming Excelerator.tech as licensor: non-transferable, royalty-free, modify + use in games allowed, but it prohibits distributing / making available the files individually or as part of another bundle or package and uploading them where others can access them as standalone files. A resource pack puts (processed) Oggs on every player's client. Hence: customer builds do not get the library until the owner confirms (`CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`), and the validator refuses a variant that would ship one library sound unchanged (needs pitch, another layer or an effect). Not legal advice.
- **Taxonomy** (data in `taxonomy.json`, applied by `classify.ts`; owner review report: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/sound-library-catalog.md`): file-name words -> synonym table (gunfire/gunshots -> gunshot, swoosh/swish -> whoosh, clapping -> applause...) -> category = first category in file order whose keywords hit the prefix words, else any word. Categories: ui_alerts 98, creatures_voices 79, music_stingers 77, environment_ambience 61, movement 56, doors_mechanisms 51, impacts_destruction 46, weapons 20, crowd_reactions 17, magic_energy 9. `music_stingers` and `magic_energy` were added to the 8 requested so musical cues and magic sounds do not land in `other` (now 0 files). Use cases (multi-valued): weapon_fire, weapon_reload, weapon_impact, melee, mob_ambient/hurt/death/attack/step, ability_cast, magic, boss_event, ui_notification, pickup_reward, block_interaction, door_mechanis
- **Search** (`library-search.ts`, pure): free text with synonym expansion (`querySynonyms`: gun -> gunshot/reload/weapon, scary -> creepy/scream/suspense/growl/..., ui -> ui_alerts) and ranking exact tag (5; 4 via a synonym) > use case / category (3) > tag prefix (2) > file-name word (1), every query word must match; filters (category, useCase, tags, durationClass, intensity, pitchBand, character, loopable, duration range), facets, pagination, `similarTo(id)` (same category, shared use cases, close descriptors).
- **Model catalog**: `services/modbuilder/sound-catalog.txt` (generated, ~23 KB): `<id> <durationClass> <useCases>` grouped by category, nothing else; `sound-catalog.json` = id -> seconds for the validator.

### 2. Audio pipeline (`lib/cyrus/sound/{dsp,measure,render,runner,host,job}.ts`, `runner.bundle.cjs`)
- **ffmpeg on node-2, isolated**: BtbN FFmpeg-Builds static release `autobuild-2026-10-09-14-16`, file `ffmpeg-n8.1.3-16-ge0a878dd70-linux64-lgpl-8.1.tar.xz`, sha256 `9ee0b516...e5e1` (matched GitHub's asset digest and the release `checksums.sha256`), extracted to `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/ffmpeg/` (`current` -> it). Binaries: ffmpeg `bcb7aa88...30d6`, ffprobe `6e048ec2...86c1`. **Licence: LGPL v3 or later** (`--enable-version3`, no `--enable-gpl`, no nonfree; `ffmpeg -L` says LGPL 3); it includes libvorbis (BSD) and libmp3lame. Only glibc is dynamic. Run as a separate process only, argv arrays, `-protocol_whitelist file` (decode) / `pipe` (encode/probe), never user filter strings; never redistributed.
- **DSP** (pure, Float64, 44.1 kHz mono): downmix, trim, gain, raised-cosine fades, pitch by resampling (cubic Hermite; speed changes with pitch like Minecraft's own `pitch`), mix at offsets, RBJ biquads (low/high/band/shelf), DC block, echo, small Schroeder reverb, silence trim, look-ahead limiter, length cap, s16 conversion, WAV writer. Render chain per variant: layers -> processing -> 30 Hz cut + DC block -> trim silence -> cap at the role's max -> edge fades -> normalise to the role's loudness target -> limiter at -1.5 dBFS. **Measurement**: sample peak, true peak (4x Hann-windowed sinc), integrated loudness (BS.1770 K-weighting, 400 ms blocks, absolute + relative gates; one ungated block for clips < 400 ms), silence ratio (10 ms windows < -50 dBFS), DC offset.
- **Runner on node-2** (`runner.ts`, bundled with esbuild to `runner.bundle.cjs`, committed; a test fails when it is stale): re-validates the specs, checks each library file's sha256 before decoding, renders, encodes `-c:a libvorbis -q:a 4 -ac 1` with `-fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact -map_metadata -1`, decodes the Ogg back and measures it; if the encoder pushed the true peak above -1 dBTP it re-renders with a lower ceiling (max 2 more passes, still deterministic).
- **Render host** (`host.ts`): `sshRenderHost()` ships the bundle once as `runner-<sha16>.cjs` into `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/sound-render/` and runs `flock -E 75 -w 90 render.lock timeout -k 5 120 nice -n 10 ionice -c2 -n7 node --max-old-space-size=768 ...` with the job on stdin (one render at a time; exit 75 = busy). Injectable (tests use a fake). `selectRenderHost(env)`: OFF unless `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` (+ optional `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER_HOST/_ROOT`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_DIR`, `CYRUS_SOUND_FFMPEG_DIR`). Audio is never rendered on the primary.
- **Determinism**: same SoundSpec + same library -> byte-identical Ogg. Verified: two real renders of the 11-file banshee set gave identical Ogg and PCM sha256 for every file, and three separate real runs built the same 1.21.11 pack (sha1 `835d969cb806ea5e31e8e47e4e238b629416aa7c`). The PCM sha256 (16-bit) is recorded too, as the reference if a future ffmpeg/libvorbis changes the encoder bytes. Goldens: synth presets + the example spec are pinned by PCM hash (computed under Node 24 on node-2).

### 3. Synth presets (`synth.ts`, params in `synth-params.ts`)
Seeded (xorshift32) and pure: `growl` (jittered saw through formant band-passes), `wail` (FM sine glide, vibrato, breath), `whoosh` (noise through a swelling band-pass), `impact` (pitch-dropping thump + noise crack), `gunshot` (crack + boom + tail + slap-back), `click`, `confirm` (two-note blip; no randomness), `magic` (gliding triad, tremolo, sparkle grains). Every param has a documented range and default; out-of-range values are clamped. (`lib/cyrus/sfx.ts`, the browser UI synth, is unrelated and unchanged.)

### 4. SoundSpec v1 (`spec.ts`; the service copy `services/modbuilder/sound-spec.js` is GENERATED from it)
`{version: 1, name, events: [{event, role, category?, subtitle (REQUIRED, 3-60 chars), variants: [{weight 1-10, layers: [1-4], processing?}]}]}` with layer `{source: "lib:<id>" | "synth:<preset>" | "silence", start, gain dB, pitch semitones, length, trimStart (library), fadeIn/fadeOut ms, seed + params (synth)}` and processing `{lowpass, highpass, reverb, echo}`. Roles set loudness band + max length (attack 2 s, death 4, fire 2.5, ability 6, hurt 1.5, spawn 4, reload 3, ui 1.5, other 6, ambient 4, step 0.6). Cost guards: 8 events/set, 4 variants, 4 layers, 60 s per set, 8 sets / 24 events / 120 s per mod, 32 KB per file. The validator returns a normalised spec that validates to itself (the render host re-validates what the portal sends). Pack keys: `<ns>:<set>.<event>`, subtitle key `subtitles.<ns>.<set>.<event>`.

### 5. Build service (`services/modbuilder/{sounds.js,prompts.js,server.js,textures.js,sound-*.json/txt}`)
- `assets.sound` (+ new `assets.library`, only meaningful with sound) from the portal; `/health` `features.assets: ["texture", "sound"]`; asset builds still never deduped. `ASSET_PROMPT_VERSION` is now `mb-assets-2026-10-10.2` (texture text unchanged).
- `SOUND_SECTION` (with library) / `SOUND_SECTION_SYNTH` appended to the system prompt only when sounds are allowed (two fixed variants, both cache per version; namespace in the user turn): format, roles, subtitles, presets + params, processing, library rules, playback with `world.playSound(location, "<ns>:<set>.<event>", SoundCategory.X, 1f, 1f)` / `player.playSound`, never vanilla keys, `entity.setSilent(true)` on a reskinned vanilla mob with the plugin playing ambient/hurt/death/attack/step itself, the 26.x Peaceful spawn guard, and the "accept the resource pack" line.
- With the library, `sound-library/catalog.txt` is placed read-only (0444) in the workspace for each AI call and removed before compiling (never in the source). Allow-list: `assets/sounds/<set>.json` only when sounds are allowed; a change without sound rights keeps the base's sound specs byte for byte. `checkWorkspaceSounds` (hard: JSON/spec/name/budgets; soft: every event played with its key, reserved namespace, no `minecraft:` keys) runs in `assetRound` beside the texture check (shared `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS`, drop-don't-ship). `assetResult.sounds: [{key, path, sha256, spec, quality (spec stage), events: [{event, key, role, category, subtitle, variants}]}]`, `keptKinds`, `downgraded[].kind`.

### 6. Portal (`lib/cyrus/assets/{plan,request,sounds,sync,sync-deps}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/textures/pack.ts`, `lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts`)
- `ASSET_PIPELINE_READY.sound = true`; gate semantics unchanged (sound: Saka + top plan create/edit; free/Katara none; keep/install/export never gated). Sounds need no item models, so 1.21.1 may have them. The service field gets `library` only with sound (texture-only requests stay byte-identical).
- `syncBuildAssets`: re-validate (`checkReturnedSound`; library sets dropped unless cleared), budgets, render via `deps.selectRenderHost`, `acceptRendered` (sha256 / OggS / mono vorbis / quality not fail; failing variants dropped, empty events dropped), `buildPack({textures, sounds})` (one pack; `assets/<ns>/sounds/<set>/<event>_<n>.ogg`, `sounds.json` with `subtitle` + weighted `sounds`, `lang/en_us.json`; min format 46 only when there are item models), Pack Loader prompt names textures and/or sounds, manifest entries `assets/sounds/<set>.json`, one `CyrusProjectAsset` kind `sound` per set (mime `application/vnd.nxeon.sound-spec+json`, provenance: spec, render status + host + tool, per file ogg/pcm sha256, measure, quality, render passes, the ledger rows of the library sounds used). No render host -> `soundRender: "off"`, specs still recorded in a revision, nothing shipped. `MbAssets.so
- NxLabs page: "Includes N custom sounds (subtitled); players accept a resource pack on join." (or not-hosted / not-rendered / could-not-build variants), dropped sounds, and "Bedrock players (Geyser/Floodgate) hear vanilla sounds...".

# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89e191ba-ed4f-44ab-bb98-634cfe568dca) # BetterModel *- Modern Bedrock model engine for Minecraft Java Edition -* [![](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/io.github.toxicity188/bettermodel-api?style=flat-square&logo=sonatype)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.github.toxicity188/bettermodel-api) [![](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/toxicity188/BetterModel/publish.yml?style=flat-square)](https://modrinth.com/plugin/bettermodel/versions) [![](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/toxicity188/BetterModel?style=flat-square&logo=github)](https://github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel/issues) [![](https://img.shields.io/bstats/servers/24237?style=flat-square)](https://bstats.org/plugin/bukkit/BetterModel/24237) [![](https://www.codefactor.io/repository/github/toxicity188/bettermodel/badge?style=flat-square)](https://www.codefactor.io/repository/github/toxicity188/bettermodel)
* * * ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a6c1a8c-6fe2-4a67-a10e-e63e40825d35) ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff515577-6a72-48ba-9943-81f00dddb375) * * * (In BlockBench / In Minecraft) # ✨ Introduction **BetterModel** is a server-based engine that provides runtime [BlockBench](https://www.blockbench.net/) model rendering & animating for Minecraft Java Edition. - Built on the `item-display` packet. - Implements **essential BlockBench elements**, including `cubes`, `meshes`, `null objects`, and `locators`. - Support for **model animations**, `Molang` expressions, and **IK** (Inverse Kinematics) rigging. - Supports **player skin models** and **custom armor**. - **Automated resource pack generation** with **zero reliance on core shaders**. - Provides support for **entity syncing**. - **Extensible API** available for integration.
In-Game Screenshots ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4e69aef-a446-4ac3-b84e-eb42fe4f069d) ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94aee9ed-9c2f-4975-92c4-3ea84ae31d24) ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb2d64ef-7b6e-4306-8c31-d92d0266dbac) ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/034dd64c-6889-4a01-961d-e69679b1c71b)
## 🚀 Key Features & Focus BetterModel aims to be a reliable engine that provides stable, high-quality animations for Paper-based high-traffic servers. - **Stability First**: We take a conservative approach to feature expansion. By avoiding the implementation of features that are difficult to maintain or have limited use cases, we focus on providing a stable API and ensuring overall operational safety. - **Performance Optimized**: Our goal is to minimize runtime computation, memory footprint, and network overhead. Through asynchronous design and optimized packet handling, we ensure the engine runs efficiently even under heavy server loads. - **Tailored for Large-scale Servers**: We provide essential features specifically designed for high-population servers and MMORPG content creation. - **Per-player Animation**: Individual animation control tailored to each player's perspective. - **Player Model Animation**: Support for sophisticated 12-limb animations based on player models. ## 📚 Wiki [![](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Wiki-181717?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel/wiki) [![](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/toxicity188/BetterModel) ## 🛠️ Build info [![](https://img.shields.io/badge/minecraft-1.21.4%7E26.3.x-8FCA5C)](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/download/server) [![](https://img.shields.io/badge/java-25%7E-ED8B00)](https://adoptium.net/) #### Build [![](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@intergrav/devins-badges@3/assets/cozy/built-with/gradle_vector.svg)](https://gradle.org/) `./gradlew build`: Builds all jars `./gradlew shadowJar`: Builds plugin jar `./gradlew javadocJar`: Builds Javadoc jar `./gradlew runServer`: Runs Paper test server with test plugin #### Library - [Kotlin stdlib](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin): modern functional programming - [semver4j](https://github.com/semver4j/semver4j): semver parser - [cloud](https://github.com/Incendo/cloud-minecraft): command - [adventure](https://github.com/PaperMC/adventure): component - [caffeine](https://github.com/ben-manes/caffeine): concurrent map cache - [DynamicUV](https://github.com/toxicity188/DynamicUV): player model - [ArmorModel](https://github.com/toxicity188/ArmorModel): armor in player model - [java-mesh](https://github.com/toxicity188/java-mesh): mesh rendering - [molang-compiler](https://github.com/Ocelot5836/molang-compiler): compiling and evaluating molang expression - [libby](https://github.com/AlessioDP/libby): runtime library downloader #### Tested Bukkit Server Platform - [Paper](https://papermc.io/downloads/paper) - [Purpur](https://purpurmc.org/download/purpur) - [Spigot](https://www.spigotmc.org/) - [Folia](https://papermc.io/downloads/folia) - [Leaf](https://www.leafmc.one/download) - [Canvas](https://canvasmc.io/downloads/canvas) #### Tested Mod Server Platform - [Fabric Loader](https://fabricmc.net/) ## 💻 API [![](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@intergrav/devins-badges@3/assets/cozy/available/maven-central_vector.svg)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.github.toxicity188/bettermodel) > [!NOTE]\ > For more detailed API specifications, please refer to our [GitHub Wiki](https://github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel/wiki/API-example).
Gradle (Kotlin) #### Release ```kotlin repositories { mavenCentral() maven("https://maven.blamejared.com/") // For transitive dependency in bettermodel-fabric maven("https://maven.nucleoid.xyz/") // For transitive dependency in bettermodel-fabric } dependencies { compileOnly("io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-bukkit-api:VERSION") // bukkit(spigot, paper, etc) api //api("io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-fabric:VERSION") // mod(fabric) } ``` #### Snapshot ```kotlin repositories { maven("https://maven.pkg.github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel") { credentials { username = YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME password = YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN } } maven("https://maven.blamejared.com/") // For transitive dependency in bettermodel-fabric maven("https://maven.nucleoid.xyz/") // For transitive dependency in bettermodel-fabric } dependencies { compileOnly("io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-bukkit-api:VERSION-SNAPSHOT") // bukkit(spigot, paper, etc) api //api("io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-fabric:VERSION-SNAPSHOT") // mod(fabric) } ```
Gradle (Groovy) #### Release ```groovy repositories { mavenCentral() maven 'https://maven.blamejared.com/' // For transitive dependency in bettermodel-fabric maven 'https://maven.nucleoid.xyz/' // For transitive dependency in bettermodel-fabric } dependencies { compileOnly 'io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-bukkit-api:VERSION' // bukkit(spigot, paper, etc) api //api 'io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-fabric:VERSION' // mod(fabric) } ``` #### Snapshot ```groovy repositories { maven { url "https://maven.pkg.github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel" credentials { username = YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME password = YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN } } maven 'https://maven.blamejared.com/' // For transitive dependency in bettermodel-fabric maven 'https://maven.nucleoid.xyz/' // For transitive dependency in bettermodel-fabric } dependencies { compileOnly 'io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-bukkit-api:VERSION-SNAPSHOT' // bukkit(spigot, paper, etc) api //api 'io.github.toxicity188:bettermodel-fabric:VERSION-SNAPSHOT' // mod(fabric) } ```
Maven #### Release ```xml central https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2 io.github.toxicity188 bettermodel-bukkit-api VERSION provided ``` #### Snapshot ```xml github https://maven.pkg.github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel io.github.toxicity188 bettermodel-api VERSION-SNAPSHOT provided io.github.toxicity188 bettermodel-bukkit-api VERSION-SNAPSHOT provided ```
Example code #### Gets some model or limb ```java BetterModel.model("demon_knight"); //A model file in BetterModel/models (for general model with saving) BetterModel.limb("steve"); //A model file in BetterModel/players (for player model with no saveing) BetterModel.modelOrNull("demon_knight"); //general model or null BetterModel.limbOrNull("steve"); //player model or null ``` #### Creates model (entity) ```java EntityTracker tracker = BetterModel.model("demon_knight") .map(r -> r.getOrCreate(BukkitAdapter.adapt(entity))) //Gets or creates entity tracker by this renderer to some entity. .orElse(null); ``` ```java EntityTracker tracker = BetterModel.model("demon_knight") .map(r -> r.create(BukkitAdapter.adapt(entity), TrackerModifier.DEFAULT, t -> t.update(TrackerUpdateAction.tint(0x0026FF)))) //Creates entity tracker with pre-spawn task. .orElse(null); ``` #### Creates model (dummy) ```java DummyTracker tracker = BetterModel.model("demon_knight") .map(r -> r.create(BukkitAdapter.adapt(location))) //Creates some dummy tracker to this location. .orElse(null); ``` ```java DummyTracker tracker = BetterModel.limb("steve") .map(r -> r.create(BukkitAdapter.adapt(location), ModelProfile.of(BukkitAdapter.adapt(player)))) //Creates some dummy tracker to this location and player's skin profile. .orElse(null); ``` #### Update some tracker's display data ```java BetterModel.model("demon_knight") .map(r -> r.create(BukkitAdapter.adapt(entity), TrackerModifier.DEFAULT, t -> { t.update(TrackerUpdateAction.tint(rgb)); //Tint t.update(TrackerUpdateAction.enchant(true), bone -> true); //Enchant with predicate })) .ifPresent(tracker -> tracker.update(TrackerUpdateAction.composite( //Composite TrackerUpdateAction.brightness(15, 15) //Brightness TrackerUpdateAction.billboard(Display.Billboard.CENTER) //Billboard ))); } ```

BetterModel pulls in dependencies at runtime—Paper's MavenLibraryResolver fetches the paper-library, while libby grabs manifest libraries like kotlin stdlib, bstats, molang-compiler, and cloud from Maven Central. Since the Test Flight netns has no internet access, I need to think about pre-populating the libraries cache directories (Paper's `libraries/` folder and libby's plugin cache) so these downloads aren't needed at startup.

This also surfaces an important production consideration: on real customer servers, BetterModel will try to download ~10 libraries from Maven Central on first boot, which requires internet access and may run into Paper's restrictions or mirror warnings around direct Maven Central usage since 1.21.x.

For a managed plugin catalog, I'd want to record a `runtimeLibraries` entry per plugin with coordinates, hashes, and paths for supply-chain pinning. Since Test Flight has no internet access, I can't just run BetterModel to observe where it caches libraries—I'll need to inspect the BetterModelLoader class and its libby usage directly via javap or string extraction on node-2 to figure out the actual library paths.

I'm thinking through how Libby handles jar relocation—it downloads libraries into the plugin's libs folder and uses jar-relocator plus ASM to produce relocated versions of dependencies like Kotlin stdlib, which adds complexity when combined with Paper's library resolver.

Since I can't run a live first-boot to pre-fetch everything with internet access, I need to figure out the exact file paths and jars Libby expects so I can pre-place them correctly, including jar-relocator and ASM themselves, so relocation can succeed entirely offline.

I'm also realizing Paper's own library resolver uses Aether's local repository semantics, where artifacts without a `_remote.repositories` marker are treated as locally installed and resolvable offline — but I still need the POM files present so Aether can compute transitive dependencies like caffeine's dependencies on jspecify and error_prone annotations.

Since the netns has no internet, I need to compute the full transitive closure myself. I'm considering writing a small Python resolver that downloads POMs, parses dependencies, and handles parent POMs and dependencyManagement, but that's getting complicated — so I'm thinking about just using Gradle on node-2 to do the resolution instead.

I'd set up a throwaway Gradle build listing those four coordinates as runtimeOnly dependencies, then have it copy the resolved runtimeClasspath jars and POMs into maven layout. I'm also wondering if I can override Paper's library repository property or point BetterModel at a local file-based maven repo instead, since I can't change its hardcoded mirror URL.

Since Aether offline mode isn't really configurable through Paper's resolver, I'll just manually compute the dependency closure for the four libraries—semver4j, dynamicuv, java-mesh, and caffeine (which pulls in jspecify and error_prone_annotations)—with a small Python script that recursively fetches POMs, handles parent POMs, and substitutes version properties.

For the libby-managed artifacts, I need the exact pinned versions from the manifest: kotlin-stdlib, bstats-bukkit plus its base module, molang-compiler from the moonflower repo, and likely cloud-paper too.

I'm also listing out the cloud command framework pieces (core, services, brigadier, bukkit), geantyref, the full adventure stack including its platform-bukkit variant under an unusual group id, and asm-tree. Libby also needs jar-relocator for relocation, and some dependencies like adventure are conditional depending on whether it's Paper or Spigot, so I need to pin down the precise set carefully.

Since getting the exact bytecode-level list manually is tedious, I'm thinking about ways to let a test flight sandbox attempt the download and report failures, but the netns has no internet access by design, so adding a proxy allowlist feels like overkill. Prefetching libraries by running BetterModel's download code outside a server isn't really feasible either. The more practical route is to iterate flights one at a time, reading the log after each failed attempt to see which library download failed, fetching that artifact into the seed directory, and repeating until the plugin enables successfully.

#!/bin/bash
# Build one Test Flight fixture plugin jar the way the build service does (javac --release N -proc:none against the
# version's resolved classpath file, reproducible `jar --date`). Runs on the build host; fixtures are trusted code.
#   build.sh <fixture-dir> <api-version> <java-home> <release 21|25> <classpath.txt> <out.jar>
set -euo pipefail
SRC="${1:?fixture dir}"; API="${2:?api-version}"; JH="${3:?java home}"; REL="${4:?release}"; CP="${5:?classpath file}"; OUT="${6:?out jar}"
W="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$W/classes"
"$JH/bin/javac" -J-Xmx768m --release "$REL" -proc:none -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$(tr -d '\n' < "$CP")" -d "$W/classes" $(find "$SRC/src" -name '*.java' | sort)
sed "s/@API@/$API/" "$SRC/plugin.yml" > "$W/classes/plugin.yml"
( cd "$W/classes" && find . -type f | sed 's#^\./##' | sort > "$W/entries" )
args=(); while read -r e; do args+=(-C "$W/classes" "$e"); done < "$W/entries"
"$JH/bin/jar" --create --file "$OUT" --date 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z "${args[@]}"
sha256sum "$OUT"

content.thinking:
Good progress: BetterModel 3.5.0 loaded the compiled banshee model correctly, and since the models directory pre-existed, the default demo models weren't extracted. But something's wrong—zombies count drops to 0 right after spawning, meaning they vanished immediately. I'm wondering if this is tied to the world spawn location in a tiny flat world causing some kind of immediate despawn.

Actually, this might be peaceful difficulty removing hostile mobs each tick, even though I thought I set difficulty to EASY. Maybe server.properties overrides it or the setDifficulty call didn't persist—I should try using a non-hostile mob as a test instead to isolate whether difficulty is the real culprit.

More likely culprit: spawn chunks were removed in 1.21.9+, so with no players online, the chunk at world spawn is actually unloaded and spawnEntity only loads it temporarily before it unloads again, killing the entity. The fix would be to add a plugin chunk ticket to keep spawn chunks loaded, since unticked chunks without a player nearby won't keep entities alive either.

That should use the vanilla force ticket, giving entity ticking. Now I'm wondering about the animation finishing late — BetterModel probably only ticks animations when there are viewers present, or the tracker paused because the mob became invalid despite trackersOpen showing 1. I'll fix the chunk loading first and check if that resolves it, then look at why build.zip is 1.36 MB even with just the banshee included.

The extra size is likely from bundled player-animation module assets (steve model). I should disable that module in the config to shrink the pack, but first let me inspect what's actually in build.zip.

Now I'm wiring creature support through server.js: adding a helper to check if creature assets are enabled on a record, exposing it through the system prompt options, allowing creature files through workspace sanitization, snapshotting specs for change-builds that lack creature rights, and including creatures in asset rounds and asset result summaries. Continuing that code pattern, I'm sketching the attack animation with play-once modifier and a sound effect, the hurt animation triggered from EntityDamageEvent with damage tinting, and the death handling tied to EntityDeathEvent -- noting uncertainty about whether BetterModel automatically closes the tracker when the entity is removed or whether the plugin needs to call close() explicitly on a delayed task.

I should document that `plugin.yml` needs a `depend: [BetterModel]` entry, that the API is compile-only and never shaded, and that only the public `kr.toxicity.model.api.*` package should be used -- plus the practice of storing trackers in a map and closing them all during onDisable.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
